lines.say: {b1}Here's a reaction: X turning into products. {b2}Now double the starting concentration. {q}If the half-life on the left is sixteen minutes, what is it on the right?
Real OCR A-level question. {pz}Pause and try it!
{rem}Quick reminder. {fo}First order means the rate equals k times the concentration of X. {hl}And half-life is the time it takes for the concentration to halve.
{go}Let's run it. {c1}The left starts at one, {dt1}and sixteen minutes later, it's down to a half.
{c2}The right starts at two. {fast}It reacts twice as fast at the start, because the rate depends on concentration. {m16}But after sixteen minutes... {h2}it's down to one. It's halved too!
{why}Why? Twice the rate, but twice as much to get rid of. They cancel out.
{m32}Keep going. Thirty-two minutes: halved again. {m48}Forty-eight: halved again. {slide}Slide the first curve along, and it's exactly the same curve.
{form}That's why, for first order, t half equals ln two over k. {nox}There's no concentration in it! {ans}So the half-life is still sixteen minutes.
{trap}Eight minutes is the trap. It only thinks about the faster rate.
